task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, runtime state collection, browser capability collection and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable browser fingerprint value rather than merely collecting raw features, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target browser fingerprint digest is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The submit route selects its live configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style, dataset state and browser capability surface are captured.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, browser-surface tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, fingerprint digest construction, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same submit interaction emits non-target prepare/audit objects carrying browser_fingerprint-like values before the target account.submit object.
The deployed bundle also contains device-probe and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target browser_fingerprint field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the encoder receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded value after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: submit-time navigator screen media timezone canvas fingerprint
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a stable compact digest of browser/device capability signals such as navigator, screen, timezone, media query and canvas rendering. It is not a request signature, state encoding, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no request proof/token/seal semantics; device-probe code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable browser fingerprint digest.
The target value is stable across email/otp input changes and changes when browser identity changes, so the target behavior is browser capability fingerprinting rather than local form-state encoding.
